newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac says no takeovers in sight.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac says no takeovers in sight.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp, one of Australia's big four banks and a key player in the mooted deregulation of the industry next year, said on Monday that it did not plan to announce major acquisitions in the near future.

"We continue to asesss acquisition opportunities as and when they arise," deputy chief financial officer Mathew Slatter told Reuters. "If we had something that was live at the moment then we would announce it," Slatter said.
He said Westpac's plan to buyback 85 million shares, announced earlier on Monday, reflected the fact that there were no immediate uses for the bank's capital.

"If there isn't perceived to be immediate opportunities for utilisation of the cash then we will consider returning it and that is the decision we have taken in this case ... to return a proportion of the capital through the five percent buyback."
The buyback announcement drove Westpac shares sharply higher, with the stock responding by rising 20 cents to a year's high of A$7.38.

Westpac managing director Bob Joss said the latest repurchase, and a 95 million buyback completed in July 1996, gave Westpac the capital strength that had allowed it to acquire Challenge Bank and Trust Bank of New Zealand over the last year.
"Mr Joss added that Westpac's capital levels were more than adequate to support business plans," the bank statement said.

While Slatter would not comment on Westpac's expansion plans, he said future takeovers or mergers in the banking and wider financial services sector would involve some degree of scrip issue. "And therefore it is not essential to have large capital reserves for acquisition purposes. We certainly don't foresee that as being essential," he said.
Slatter said Westpac could call on substantial resources from international capital markets if it wanted to pursue a major takeover. -- Ian Pemberton 61-2 9373-1800
